newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end higher, take heart from Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end higher, take heart from Wall St.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended sharply higher on Monday as the positive opening on Wall Street helped Spanish shares to set record highs on both indices.
Traders were bullish, saying they saw buying interest on every dip and the market is not looking for a consolidation.
"Everybody wants to stay in. There's no offer of shares from domestic or foreign investors," one dealer said.
The general index ended up 2.4 percent at 525.85 points, while Ibex-35 gained 141 points or 2.4 percent, breaking resistance at 6,059.93 points.
"Stocks are still offering good value at these levels. That's why there's no paper and everybody wants to stay in," another Madrid-based dealer added.
Trade volume was thin at 95 billion pesetas.

"At present there are more risks in selling than in holding shares. If you sell, the risk is to be left out of further rallies. If you hold, at worst you can suffer small profit-taking," another dealer added.
Among banks, Banesto jumped 8.5 percent, while Popular and Santander rose 2.6 percent. Telefonica was in line with the broader market, up 2.4 percent, Repsol was flat at 6,100.
